newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called up amid firm cash, maintenance.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called up amid firm cash, maintenance.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Thursday amid talk of stronger cash prices and maintenance in the Southwest, market sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.505 to $2.52 after settling to the downside at $2.472 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, September traded 0.7 cent firmer at $2.479.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked about 10 cents higher at $2.52-2.58.

Technical traders pegged key September resistance at the contract high and double top at $2.605, with further selling likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was seen at $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas inventories rose last week by 78 bcf, in line with expectations at 70-80 bcf. Eastern stocks increased by 62 bcf and remained 35 bcf, or three percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage, which gained two bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by two percent. Stocks in the producing region, which rose 14 bcf on the week, were still 25 percent above last year.

In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded more than 10 cents to the low-$2.40s. Midcon pipes tumbled a similar amount to the low-to-mid $2.30s. New York city gate gas was talked more than 10 cents lower in the low-$2.60s.

Warmer weather is headed toward the Northeast and Midwest, with above-normal temperatures forecast for this weekend. However, cooler air is expected to cover most of the U.S. early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
